symptom: `drop entity Shop.Customer` reported "Dropped entity" and mx check then failed CE1613 "The selected association 'Shop.Order_Customer' no longer exists." at Access rule of entity 'Shop.Order'; the same across modules (`drop entity Crm.Contact` leaving Shop.Order_Contact in Shop.Order's rule), and for the FROM end of a cross-module OWNER Both association (`drop entity Crm.Lead` leaving Crm.Lead_Order on its TO entity Shop.Order). `drop association Crm.Lead_Order` left the same entry, and `update security` printed "All entity access rules are up to date" over it (ako/mxcli#1449, mendixlabs/mxcli#1551).
cause: Two gaps. (1) execDropEntity called DeleteEntity, which cascades the associations away in every module, and reconciled nothing; execDropAssociation reconciled only the DECLARING module, though under OWNER Both a cross-module association is a member of its TO entity in another module. (2) ReconcileMemberAccesses kept every association reference qualified by another module (the 'preserve what cannot be checked' branch for associations inherited across modules, #758), so even a reconcile of the right module could not remove an entry for an association that no longer exists anywhere.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_entities.go (associationMemberModules, read before the delete), mdl/executor/cmd_associations.go (reconcileModulesAccess, now behind create/alter/drop association and drop entity); mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_security_write.go (scanProjectAssociations records what every module declares; staleForeignRef)
insight: Which modules to reconcile is not 'the module written': a rule naming an association lives on the FROM entity (the declaring module, or ANOTHER module when the dropped entity is the TO end of a cross-module association) and under OWNER Both on the TO entity too — and that set must be read BEFORE the delete, while the associations exist. 'Preserve what cannot be checked' was right for its case and had quietly widened to every foreign reference: existence in the declaring module is checkable from the same scan the reconcile already did for incoming associations, and 'not declared' is a positive finding, not an unknown. Keep the boundary narrow — System (virtual domain model) and absent modules stay preserved, and an existing association on a specialization of another module's entity stays (control test). A single MDL script is a weak repro here: the end-of-program reconcile repairs the same-module and FROM-side cases on the old binary, so only the OWNER Both one shows in a combined script — run the drop as its own script to see all three. Measured on mxbuild 11.13.0: baseline 1 CE1613 per drop, fixed 0; `update security` on a project broken by the old binary now repairs it.
